question.text: Let $\mathrm{S}, \mathrm{T}, \mathrm{U}$ be three non-void sets and $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{T}, \mathrm{g}: \mathrm{T} \rightarrow \mathrm{U}$ and composed mapping $\mathrm{gof}: \mathrm{S} \rightarrow U$ be defined. Let $\mathrm{gof}$ be injective mapping. Then

solution.text:
Let, $x_1, x_2 \in S$ and $f\left(x_1\right)=f\left(x_2\right)$
$\Rightarrow g \circ f\left(x_1\right)=g\left(f\left(x_1\right)\right)=g\left(f\left(x_2\right)\right)=g$ of $\left(x_2\right)$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}_1=\mathrm{x}_2$ (as gof is injective)
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is obviously injective.
